defects.original:
The hearing room contained six chairs for the public and three more that had been borrowed from the marriage office. Lena counted them while the clerk tried to find a frame large enough to dry the register without flattening its spine. A crowd stood beyond the open door, listening to the scrape of furniture as though proceedings had already begun. Lena entered the town hall before the hearing began. Her wrist had stiffened during the walk from the bridge. The nurse wrapped Lena’s bruised wrist in a clean bandage. The nurse told her to stop using it to hold heavy books, a reasonable instruction that made the room's shortage of tables newly offensive. Ivo fetched a small stand. Tomas opened the shutters. Nobody mentioned the missing inspector until the clerk read his name among the officials who had been expected to attend.

[noncontiguous passage]

“Rook asked me to duplicate the entry,” Ivo said. This time Ivo did not retreat into a narrower meaning. He described the inspector telling him to add a line so a second charge would not appear as a second visit. Lena asked him whether he had understood the purpose. He said he had understood enough to dislike the instruction and not enough to refuse wages he needed. The duplicate entry concealed a second docking fee. The fee book showed one payment in the proper column and another written into a private reconciliation sheet. Lena knew the duplicate entry had been made to conceal an unlawful docking fee. She did not turn that knowledge into a claim that every inspection had been corrupt. The evidence concerned this fee, this entry, and the missing transfer. The public could demand a wider inquiry without pretending that the wider inquiry had already happened. The clerk copied her qualification into the hearing minutes, although it made the sentence longer.

[noncontiguous passage]

When the clerk adjourned, the crowd stayed to compare sums on the displayed copies. Tomas asked whether the archive should open that afternoon despite the damaged shutter. Lena said the reading table was safe if the upper corridor remained closed until repair. Tomas returned to the archive to open it for the public. He carried the posted access conditions where anyone could see them. The red marker was installed at Merrow Quay for the new survey. The watch officer sent it with two workers and a new warning board, separating the channel survey from the bridge hazard at last. Lena watched their progress from the hall window. Beyond the quay, a boat moved through the thinning fog. Lena could only guess who had left a boat moving beyond the fog. It might have carried a witness or nothing more interesting than another crew trying to reach home. She recorded its direction because she had seen that much. She left its owner blank because the temptation to complete the line was not evidence.

[noncontiguous passage]

The watch officer brought the sealed minutes back for one last reading. Lena corrected a sentence that made Ivo's report sound like something she had witnessed and another that implied the bell could determine the tide. He accepted both changes without argument. Outside, someone tested the lever under supervision. The bell sounded exactly once, an ordinary piece of metal moved by an ordinary hand. People at the window turned towards it. Lena wrote the time beside the test instruction and felt, for the first time since arriving, that the sound had a proportion she could understand. It could warn a boat or summon a watchman. It could not by itself explain a death, prove a payment, or make the sea obey a line in a book. The officer sealed the corrected copy while she held the paper flat with her uninjured hand.
